messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Fwd: use renjin for hadoop and spark programming
parts:
Hi Jiessie,

Hope you don't mind, I'm copying the contributors group on this because I think there is a wider interest. 

The JRMapReduceCooker is looking good! To make it easy to reuse, perhaps we could split it into two maven projects -- the first jar with R and java support routines, and the second a maven plugin that handles the packaging of the user's mapper/reducer into a jar for deployment to hadoop.

I think ultimately we need a generic util in renjin core that generates a class file stub which implements an interface or abstract class by calling out to R scripts. It shouldn't be so hard to do with libasm, may be you could give a try?

Have you been able to work around national restrictions and access the google repo? Again, if you're still having problems we can convert the repo to git and then create a mirror on github where you can commit.

Best,

Alex
 
---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Jiessie Cao <jiess...@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, Dec 12, 2011 at 2:07 PM
Subject: Re: use renjin for hadoop and spark programming
To: "Bertram, Alexander" <al...@bedatadriven.com>


Hi Alex,
       I have not implemented the API in R,
      for now you must save the map function and reduce function into  tow files, and speciafy the K1,V1,K2,V2,K3,V3, and run org.cgcl.lsde.jrmapreduce.core.JRMapReduceCooker  to genetator the code and cook the jar. then you can hadoop jar your jar to run.
      (for the third party jar such as google  and renjin-core, I haven't package it in the jar)  So for simple ,you can just put the renjin-swing-sample-0.1.2-SNAPSHOT.jar in the $Hadoop_HOME/lib at every tasknode.  In this way the jar file will be small enough to transfer.
    I use the generated wrapperd jar  to compare with the original hadoop-example.jar to count the same file.
     wrapped.jar takes 37 seconds , the original file takes 30s (with much bigger dataset this performance maybe relative small.)
    The Renjin engine startup takes 1-2 seconds per time to interpreter the initialization the R environment for every task. I think this will solved by your compiler later.
     
next step, I imagine that user can use R file alone or just type the code in the interpreter .

A question here,  when you type the mapreduce code in the interpreter, and sumbit, because i want to use the renjin engine to eval the R code, so I want to exact the code from map and value closures,but I only can get the SEXP after parse, and is it possible to the binary closure to transfer and excute directly.

And a listener should be implmented to monitor the progress of mapreduce job so the you can fetch the result from hdfs ASAP.
 
I wish the R user will need not know anything about Writable type (except for the context$write() method), they can use R internal type to write code.the wrapper will finish the type conversion

for the Writable interface converter, I use two times converter for input and output
when I read the source code of hadoop, i found most type it wrappered a Primitive Type as it's value field ((int,bool,byte[]  etc.))

 1.  Writable ---> simple Primitive Type
 2. renjin have implemented the Primitive Type to R object( such as charactor,list etc)
 then the R user can write R code without thinking of the inputType
for ouput,
 1. R object ->java primitive object
 2. java primitive object  -->writable
 then the R user can write R code without thinking of the outputType

with above converter , R use can just use the R code to write their code without knowing the writeable java object.

But when you write a special writable with a special object as it's value, then the value will transfer into the R as a ObjectFrame, then the R user must know how to use it itself. if HashMap as  the value of a MapWritable Object, then the use should know use map$put(foo,bar) by themself,

thank you!  wish your best advices!



On Mon, Dec 12, 2011 at 5:27 PM, Bertram, Alexander <al...@bedatadriven.com> wrote:
Hi Jiessie,

This is great news! 
Let me take a closer look at the package and will send you detailed feedback this week. I think keeping it as a seperate project is a good idea. For the changes to renjin core, let me know if you succeed in getting access to google code svn, otherwise we can look at setting up a mirror on github that you can commit to. 

For the Writable interface, have you thought about setting up a hadoop converter for SEXP ? SEXP graphs can be serialized to a byte stream with DatefileReader and DatafileWriter. 

What do you think about submitting jobs to hadoop interactively? With your cooker, could you imagine something like :

map <- function(key, value, context) { ... }
reduce <- function(key, value, context) { ... }

submitJob(map, reduce) 

?

Ok, good luck with your exams and talk with you later!

Best,
Alex


On Sun, Dec 11, 2011 at 4:47 AM, Jiessie Cao <jiess...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Alex,
   I have finished a prototype for renjin on Hadoop, wordcount in R can work well.
   Given the map.r and reduce.r, with 3 pairs Writable type K1,V1,K2,V2,K3,V3
  map :<K1,V1>--->list<K2,V2> 
  combiner: <K2,list<V2>>--->list<K2,V2> 
  reducer:<K2,list<V2>>--->list<K2,V2> 
  MapperWrapper\ReducerWapper\JobRunnerWrapper will generate the mapper\reducer\jobrunner,and with map.r reduce.r added , they will be made into a jar which can run on hadoop,  take mapper as a example:
 
  1.In java map method ,the input key and value are java Writable Type,firstly they canbe convert to primitive Type in R by Converters.
  2.wrapper the Context class,  and delegate the write method, which accept a  R2Java auto-Convertable primitive type(such as Logical-->boolean character->String and so on), so that you can wirte the map.r with any R type ,
but  only remember to context$write(rk2,rv2),rk2 and rv2 are the convertable type with Writable <K2,V2>.
such as org.apache.hadoop.io.Text can be constructed by byte[] and String. so contextWrapper will overload the write method with both these type , when call the context$write(rk2,rv2) in R, it can be auto-converted and binding to the most matachable overload.
     And WrapperedContext Class will wrapper the R primitive Type into Java Writable Class and use original context.write(K2,V2)


 
  3.engine.put("context",myWrappercontext)   value,context...  and  getResourceAsStream() from jar to get the map.r, and eval(reader)

  there are really many things to do and test, as it just use renjin,I think it is better to make a project out of renjin.
  For renjin, I made some modifies,as the reason of network forbidden in China(some google services works not well) ,I can't  get the svn commit key in google code,  as for the modified code for renjin, i will test and then submit when I can acquire the commit code
and I use sourceforge as my temporary source control service because it's fast for me. I submit my renjin-on-hadoop at sourceforge.
 
  you can check out the code  with
 
  svn checkout svn://svn.code.sf.net/p/jronhadoop/code/trunk jronhadoop-code

  you can use the  org.cgcl.lsde.jrmapreduce.core.JRMapReduceCooker to cook the jar with specified map.r and reduce.r
 
 the abstract model will be improved for more use case.
 
 Next week,an important exam is coming to me,I will prepare for it. So I will write more documents on jr-on-hadoop next weekend.

  I have a plan to make renjin to support many JVM based architecture for large scale data process such as hadoop,spark(with Closure),Storm,S4,etc.
 Benefit for the R on jvm, many type conversion are easy and fast then google protobuffer serilization and Streaming\pipe mechanism,  and I will do some performance test for jronhadoop with RHIPE  and RHadoop. 

  Waiting for you best advices, thank you!




 
 

 

On Thu, Dec 8, 2011 at 4:14 PM, Bertram, Alexander <al...@bedatadriven.com> wrote:
Hi Jessie,

Yes, I think you've hit on a really important point-- automatic conversion may not always be desired. I think your solution is better. What we can further do is to list the Java class and implemented interfaces in the 'class' attribute, so that you could write R functions like this:

as.character.java.util.Collection <- function(x) {
  vector <- character(0)
  for(i in 0:(x$size() - 1)) {
     vector[i] <- x$get(i)$toString()
   }
}

`[.java.util.Collection` <- function(x, i) {
   x$get(i-1)
}

length.java.util.Collection <- function(x) {
  x$size()
}

What do you think?

Great to hear about the hfds/mapreduce code, were you able to use the HDFS plugin for Apache VFS ? 

I will add you as a contributor to renjin directly, just start submitting code and we can always review it together once its in the repo. Retrieve your password here:

http://code.google.com/p/renjin/source/checkout

Best,

Alex


On Wed, Dec 7, 2011 at 11:54 AM, Jiessie Cao <jiess...@gmail.com> wrote:
thank you, I have implemented StringArrayConverter  by myself ,too.

Besides of that, I noticed the following case is useful.
#when construct, str1 will be a Environment with a String ObjectFrame,and we can use the split method in java

>str1<-String$new()  

#but str2 will be a character directly, and lose the java banding(at most time, the binding is not necessary)

>str2<-str1$toString()


As above case, except for constructor , the primitive Type will be converted automatically into R type.
at most case, this auto-converter is useful, and somtimes "str1" binding with the java type as an Environment is useful.
(of course,for special Object it will be a Objectframe with binding info)

 I think when user construct a primitive Object in Java, maybe he want to keep the java binding without auto-converter.
and if he want to convert it into R object , he can use as.character\as.double etc.

I have overload the as.character(Environment) primitives method,so you can use
>str1<-Double$new("23")   
>str2<-as.double(str1)      (also you can use str2<-str1$doubleValue())

 besides I have done some job for the hdfs api and mapreduce code generater. with more test cases and debug, this weekend i will send patches to you for more advices, thanks!


Best,

Jiessie




On Tue, Dec 6, 2011 at 4:11 AM, Bertram, Alexander <al...@bedatadriven.com> wrote:
Hi Jiessie,

First, I've updated renjin so that you can pass R values directly to array parameters, for example:

import(myclass)$main( c("a", "b", "c") )

As for the formatting, I believe the profile is correct-- but there may still be some files that are inconsistent; feel free to commit corrections!

Best,

Alex

parts:
Thanks for your foward!

Yes,I think a generic util to generate the class file directly is more meanful!

For now, I just copy the *.r files to the jar ,but time wasted by the initialization of RenjinScriptEngine Context at every map or reduce task,because renjin should load and inteperte all their base R packages. Compiling the *.r into class files with wrappered interface or abstract class will got much better performance. By this way, I think it's much easier to supprort other large scale data process infrastrcure more than just hadoop, surpporting Twitter Storm and Berkeley Spark are also on my working list.

For google code repo,I can access it by VPN and will merge the code ASAP.

But I am not familar with the compiler, I will read your code and try to do it, any suggestion for getting started?  Thanks!
